# Savi Saluwadana

> Savi Saluwadana is a software, AI systems and platform engineer based in Sri Lanka. His public engineering work spans Go backends, multi-tenant operational software, Kubernetes and developer-platform workflows, MCP integrations, PostgreSQL, Next.js and production-minded system design.

## Selected public work

### DevRelOS
Repository: https://github.com/savisaluwadana/DevRelOS

An open developer-relations operating system for developer-signal discovery, community and content workflows, developer feedback, campaigns, media workflows and measurable outcomes. The current self-hosted beta uses a Next.js operator dashboard, Go API and workers, PostgreSQL and an authenticated MCP server. The architecture emphasizes provider interfaces, source provenance, approval-gated side effects, RBAC, observable automation and a single authoritative system of record.

### Property Management OS
Repository: https://github.com/RealEstateSassApplication/property-management-OS

A multi-tenant rental operations platform covering properties, units, owners, tenants, occupancies, leases, rent, maintenance, documents, notifications and controlled agent-assisted operations. The system uses Next.js, a Go modular monolith, PostgreSQL, OIDC/JWT authentication, organization-scoped RBAC, S3-compatible storage, a transactional notification outbox, a Go worker, OpenAPI contracts and an MCP server that calls the authenticated HTTP API rather than accessing the database directly.

### RapidReach
Repository: https://github.com/savisaluwadana/RapidReachBloWebsite

A developer publication and developer-tool discovery product built with Next.js, TypeScript, MongoDB and Vercel Blob. It includes editorial workflows, comments, likes, search, tool profiles, media uploads and structured discovery surfaces including JSON-LD, sitemap.xml, robots.txt, feed.xml, llms.txt and public APIs.

### OpenChoreo ecosystem
Project: https://openchoreo.dev/
Repository: https://github.com/openchoreo/openchoreo

Contributor work around open-source platform engineering, developer-facing workflows, documentation, technical content and community enablement across Kubernetes, Backstage, MCP and internal developer platform concepts. A recurring architectural focus is keeping the developer portal as the connected experience layer while platform orchestration and lifecycle control remain behind explicit platform APIs.

## Engineering principles
- Keep domain rules authoritative on the server.
- Prefer one clear system of record before adding parallel state systems.
- Treat agents as authenticated clients, not privileged back doors.
- Make automation observable and externally consequential actions inspectable.
- Use platform abstractions to reduce friction without making systems impossible to debug.
- Add distributed infrastructure when the workload requires it, not for appearance.
